{"parentUuid":"6f0b186f-ccce-4641-b335-66d29804672a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_qh8lu3kzp71yp9u8dgnudsbd","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp1/b/src/io.rs","content":"//! Injectable I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The repository talks only to the [`Vfs`] trait. Two implementations exist:\n//!\n//! * [`RealVfs`] — a real directory on disk: `pwrite` + `fsync`, the\n//!   production backend used by the HTTP server.\n//! * [`SimVfs`] — an in-memory media model that reproduces the durability\n//!   boundary of a page-cache OS: `pwrite` only touches a dirty layer; bytes\n//!   become durable when `sync` is called. A [`CrashPolicy`] can \"cut the\n//!   power\" at any [`CrashPoint`], optionally retaining only a prefix of the\n//!   in-flight write (torn page / half-page write). After a crash a new\n//!   `SimVfs` is \"rebooted\" from the same durable [`SimMedia`], exactly like\n//!   reopening a directory after power loss.\n//!\n//! Durability model assumed (and what the tests exercise):\n//! * a single `pwrite` may survive torn — any prefix can land, the rest is\n//!   lost;\n//! * bytes written but never `sync`ed may be lost entirely;\n//!   `sync_all` is a barrier — everything before it is durable, and the\n//!   superblock is only written *after* the data sync barrier, which is what\n//!   makes the publish order safe.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// The three files a repository consists of.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum FileId {\n    Data,\n    SbA,\n    SbB,\n}\n\nimpl FileId {\n    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FileId::Data => crate::format::DATA_FILE,\n            FileId::SbA => crate::format::SB_FILE[0],\n            FileId::SbB => crate::format::SB_FILE[1],\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Points in the commit protocol at which power can be cut.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CrashPoint {\n    /// Before any byte of the new data record is written.\n    DataWriteBegin,\n    /// After the data pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    DataWriteEnd,\n    /// At the data fsync call (write still dirty).\n    DataSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the data fsync returns.\n    DataSyncEnd,\n    /// Before any byte of the new superblock page is written.\n    RootWriteBegin,\n    /// After the superblock pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    RootWriteEnd,\n    /// At the superblock fsync call (page still dirty).\n    RootSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the superblock fsync returns.\n    RootSyncEnd,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPoint {\n    pub const ALL: [CrashPoint; 8] = [\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd,\n    ];\n\n    fn file(self) -> FileId {\n        use CrashPoint::*;\n        match self {\n            DataWriteBegin | DataWriteEnd | DataSyncBegin | DataSyncEnd => FileId::Data,\n            RootWriteBegin | RootWriteEnd | RootSyncBegin | RootSyncEnd => FileId::SbA, // slot chosen per-commit\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// How torn the in-flight write is when power is cut mid-write.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Torn {\n    /// No byte survives (write never reached the platter).\n    None,\n    /// Exactly the first half of the write survives.\n    Half,\n    /// A short prefix survives (137 bytes of the 4 KiB page; for data records\n    /// it is clamped inside the record header, i.e. the header itself tears).\n    Short,\n}\n\n/// \"Cut power\" once, at the given point, with the given torn-write behaviour.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CrashPolicy {\n    pub at: CrashPoint,\n    pub torn: Torn,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPolicy {\n    pub fn new(at: CrashPoint, torn: Torn) -> Self {\n        CrashPolicy { at, torn }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum IoError {\n    /// OS-level I/O failure (real backend), or use after a simulated crash.\n    Io(String),\n    /// The configured crash policy fired: the process \"lost power\". Any\n    /// further operation on this VFS instance returns the same error; reboot\n    /// with [`SimVfs::reopen`].\n    SimulatedCrash,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for IoError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            IoError::Io(s) => write!(f, \"io error: {s}\"),\n            IoError::SimulatedCrash => write!(f, \"simulated crash (power lost)\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for IoError {}\n\npub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, IoError>;\n\n/// Minimal storage interface needed by the repository. All writes are\n/// positional (`pwrite` semantics: no file-position mutation) and durability\n/// is explicit via [`Vfs::sync`].\npub trait Vfs {\n    /// Create the file if it does not exist, then write `data` at `offset`.\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Durably persist all previously written bytes of one file.\n    fn sync(&mut self, id: FileId) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Durably persist directory-entry changes (newly created files).\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Read the whole durable file, or `None` if it does not exist.\n    fn read(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;\n    fn truncate(&mut self, id: FileId, len: u64) -> Result<()>;\n    fn exists(&self, id: FileId) -> bool;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Real filesystem backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct RealVfs {\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl RealVfs {\n    pub fn open(dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self> {\n        let dir = dir.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        Ok(RealVfs { dir })\n    }\n\n    fn path(&self, id: FileId) -> PathBuf {\n        self.dir.join(id.name())\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<File> {\n        OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(self.path(id))\n            .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for RealVfs {\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))\n            .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        f.write_all(data).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        // drop without fsync: bytes sit in the page cache, exactly like the\n        // dirty layer in the simulator.\n        drop(f);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self, id: FileId) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.sync_all().map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = File::open(&self.dir).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        f.sync_all().map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        match File::open(self.path(id)) {\n            Ok(mut f) => {\n                let mut buf = Vec::new();\n                f.read_to_end(&mut buf)\n                    .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n                Ok(Some(buf))\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(IoError::Io(e.to_string())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn truncate(&mut self, id: FileId, len: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.set_len(len).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn exists(&self, id: FileId) -> bool {\n        self.path(id).exists()\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting in-memory backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Durable media: what survives a reboot. One byte vector per existing file.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct SimMedia {\n    files: HashMap<FileId, Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl SimMedia {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SimMedia::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_len(&self, id: FileId) -> u64 {\n        self.files.get(&id).map(|v| v.len() as u64).unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_bytes(&self, id: FileId) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.files.get(&id).map(|v| v.as_slice())\n    }\n}\n\ntype Segments = Vec<(u64, Vec<u8>)>;\n\npub struct SimVfs {\n    durable: SimMedia,\n    /// Unsynced writes per file: ordered (offset, bytes) segments.\n    dirty: HashMap<FileId, Segments>,\n    policy: CrashPolicy,\n    crashed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl SimVfs {\n    pub fn fresh(policy: CrashPolicy) -> Self {\n        SimVfs {\n            durable: SimMedia::new(),\n            dirty: HashMap::new(),\n            policy,\n            crashed: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// \"Reboot\" over the same media with a new policy (use\n    /// `CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd`/`Torn::None`, i.e. no further crash, for\n    /// recovery verification).\n    pub fn reopen(self, policy: CrashPolicy) -> Self {\n        SimVfs {\n            durable: self.durable,\n            dirty: HashMap::new(), // page cache is cold after power loss\n            policy,\n            crashed: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Consume the durable media (for inspection / cross-instance tests).\n    pub fn into_media(self) -> SimMedia {\n        self.durable\n    }\n\n    /// Durable file length (what recovery would see after a crash).\n    pub fn durable_len(&self, id: FileId) -> u64 {\n        self.durable.file_len(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Copy of durable file bytes.\n    pub fn durable_bytes(&self, id: FileId) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.durable.file_bytes(id).map(|b| b.to_vec())\n    }\n\n    /// Directly overwrite durable media, bypassing the dirty layer. Used by\n    /// tests to craft corruption (bit flips, garbage pages, OOB pointers).\n    pub fn corrupt_durable(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        let v = self\n            .durable\n            .files\n            .entry(id)\n            .or_default();\n        let end = (offset as usize) + bytes.len();\n        if v.len() < end {\n            v.resize(end, 0);\n        }\n        v[offset as usize..end].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n    }\n\n    fn check_alive(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.crashed {\n            Err(IoError::SimulatedCrash)\n        } else {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn merge(durable: &mut SimMedia, id: FileId, off: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        let v = durable.files.entry(id).or_default();\n        let end = off as usize + bytes.len();\n        if v.len() < end {\n            v.resize(end, 0);\n        }\n        v[off as usize..end].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n    }\n\n    /// Apply the configured crash policy at `point` for a write to `file`.\n    /// `seg` is the in-flight write `(offset, bytes)` whose prefix may be\n    /// retained as a torn write.\n    fn crash(&mut self, point: CrashPoint, file: FileId, seg: Option<(u64, &[u8])>) -> Result<()> {\n        if point != self.policy.at {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // What survives: either nothing, or a prefix of the in-flight write.\n        if let Some((off, bytes)) = seg {\n            if self.policy.torn != Torn::None && !bytes.is_empty() {\n                let n = match self.policy.torn {\n                    Torn::None => 0,\n                    Torn::Half => bytes.len() / 2,\n                    Torn::Short => 137.min(bytes.len().saturating_sub(1)),\n                };\n                if n > 0 {\n                    Self::merge(&mut self.durable, file, off, &bytes[..n]);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Power is lost: the entire page cache (all dirty segments, of every\n        // file) is discarded.\n        self.dirty.clear();\n        self.crashed = true;\n        Err(IoError::SimulatedCrash)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for SimVfs {\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: Injectable I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The repository talks only to the [`Vfs`] trait. Two implementations exist:\n//!\n//! * [`RealVfs`] — a real directory on disk: `pwrite` + `fsync`, the\n//!   production backend used by the HTTP server.\n//! * [`SimVfs`] — an in-memory media model that reproduces the durability\n//!   boundary of a page-cache OS: `pwrite` only touches a dirty layer; bytes\n//!   become durable when `sync` is called. A [`CrashPolicy`] can \"cut the\n//!   power\" at any [`CrashPoint`], optionally retaining only a prefix of the\n//!   in-flight write (torn page / half-page write). After a crash a new\n//!   `SimVfs` is \"rebooted\" from the same durable [`SimMedia`], exactly like\n//!   reopening a directory after power loss.\n//!\n//! Durability model assumed (and what the tests exercise):\n//! * a single `pwrite` may survive torn — any prefix can land, the rest is\n//!   lost;\n//! * bytes written but never `sync`ed may be lost entirely;\n//!   `sync_all` is a barrier — everything before it is durable, and the\n//!   superblock is only written *after* the data sync barrier, which is what\n//!   makes the publish order safe.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// The three files a repository consists of.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum FileId {\n    Data,\n    SbA,\n    SbB,\n}\n\nimpl FileId {\n    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FileId::Data => crate::format::DATA_FILE,\n            FileId::SbA => crate::format::SB_FILE[0],\n            FileId::SbB => crate::format::SB_FILE[1],\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Points in the commit protocol at which power can be cut.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CrashPoint {\n    /// Before any byte of the new data record is written.\n    DataWriteBegin,\n    /// After the data pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    DataWriteEnd,\n    /// At the data fsync call (write still dirty).\n    DataSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the data fsync returns.\n    DataSyncEnd,\n    /// Before any byte of the new superblock page is written.\n    RootWriteBegin,\n    /// After the superblock pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    RootWriteEnd,\n    /// At the superblock fsync call (page still dirty).\n    RootSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the superblock fsync returns.\n    RootSyncEnd,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPoint {\n    pub const ALL: [CrashPoint; 8] = [\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd,\n    ];\n\n    fn file(self) -> FileId {\n        use CrashPoint::*;\n        match self {\n            DataWriteBegin | DataWriteEnd | DataSyncBegin | DataSyncEnd => FileId::Data,\n            RootWriteBegin | RootWriteEnd | RootSyncBegin | RootSyncEnd => FileId::SbA, // slot chosen per-commit\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// How torn the in-flight write is when power is cut mid-write.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Torn {\n    /// No byte survives (write never reached the platter).\n    None,\n    /// Exactly the first half of the write survives.\n    Half,\n    /// A short prefix survives (137 bytes of the 4 KiB page; for data records\n    /// it is clamped inside the record header, i.e. the header itself tears).\n    Short,\n}\n\n/// \"Cut power\" once, at the given point, with the given torn-write behaviour.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CrashPolicy {\n    pub at: CrashPoint,\n    pub torn: Torn,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPolicy {\n    pub fn new(at: CrashPoint, torn: Torn) -> Self {\n        CrashPolicy { at, torn }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum IoError {\n    /// OS-level I/O failure (real backend), or use after a simulated crash.\n    Io(String),\n    /// The configured crash policy fired: the process \"lost power\". Any\n    /// further operation on this VFS instance returns the same error; reboot\n    /// with [`SimVfs::reopen`].\n    SimulatedCrash,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for IoError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            IoError::Io(s) => write!(f, \"io error: {s}\"),\n            IoError::SimulatedCrash => write!(f, \"simulated crash (power lost)\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for IoError {}\n\npub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, IoError>;\n\n/// Minimal storage interface needed by the repository. All writes are\n/// positional (`pwrite` semantics: no file-position mutation) and durability\n/// is explicit via [`Vfs::sync`].\npub trait Vfs {\n    /// Create the file if it does not exist, then write `data` at `offset`.\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Durably persist all previously written bytes of one file.\n    fn sync(&mut self, id: FileId) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Durably persist directory-entry changes (newly created files).\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Read the whole durable file, or `None` if it does not exist.\n    fn read(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;\n    fn truncate(&mut self, id: FileId, len: u64) -> Result<()>;\n    fn exists(&self, id: FileId) -> bool;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Real filesystem backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct RealVfs {\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl RealVfs {\n    pub fn open(dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self> {\n        let dir = dir.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        Ok(RealVfs { dir })\n    }\n\n    fn path(&self, id: FileId) -> PathBuf {\n        self.dir.join(id.name())\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<File> {\n        OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(self.path(id))\n            .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for RealVfs {\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))\n            .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        f.write_all(data).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        // drop without fsync: bytes sit in the page cache, exactly like the\n        // dirty layer in the simulator.\n        drop(f);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self, id: FileId) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.sync_all().map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = File::open(&self.dir).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        f.sync_all().map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        match File::open(self.path(id)) {\n            Ok(mut f) => {\n                let mut buf = Vec::new();\n                f.read_to_end(&mut buf)\n                    .map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n                Ok(Some(buf))\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(IoError::Io(e.to_string())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn truncate(&mut self, id: FileId, len: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let f = self.open_write(id)?;\n        f.set_len(len).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    fn exists(&self, id: FileId) -> bool {\n        self.path(id).exists()\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting in-memory backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Durable media: what survives a reboot. One byte vector per existing file.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct SimMedia {\n    files: HashMap<FileId, Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl SimMedia {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SimMedia::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_len(&self, id: FileId) -> u64 {\n        self.files.get(&id).map(|v| v.len() as u64).unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_bytes(&self, id: FileId) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.files.get(&id).map(|v| v.as_slice())\n    }\n}\n\ntype Segments = Vec<(u64, Vec<u8>)>;\n\npub struct SimVfs {\n    durable: SimMedia,\n    /// Unsynced writes per file: ordered (offset, bytes) segments.\n    dirty: HashMap<FileId, Segments>,\n    policy: CrashPolicy,\n    crashed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl SimVfs {\n    pub fn fresh(policy: CrashPolicy) -> Self {\n        SimVfs {\n            durable: SimMedia::new(),\n            dirty: HashMap::new(),\n            policy,\n            crashed: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// \"Reboot\" over the same media with a new policy (use\n    /// `CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd`/`Torn::None`, i.e. no further crash, for\n    /// recovery verification).\n    pub fn reopen(self, policy: CrashPolicy) -> Self {\n        SimVfs {\n            durable: self.durable,\n            dirty: HashMap::new(), // page cache is cold after power loss\n            policy,\n            crashed: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Consume the durable media (for inspection / cross-instance tests).\n    pub fn into_media(self) -> SimMedia {\n        self.durable\n    }\n\n    /// Durable file length (what recovery would see after a crash).\n    pub fn durable_len(&self, id: FileId) -> u64 {\n        self.durable.file_len(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Copy of durable file bytes.\n    pub fn durable_bytes(&self, id: FileId) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.durable.file_bytes(id).map(|b| b.to_vec())\n    }\n\n    /// Directly overwrite durable media, bypassing the dirty layer. Used by\n    /// tests to craft corruption (bit flips, garbage pages, OOB pointers).\n    pub fn corrupt_durable(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        let v = self\n            .durable\n            .files\n            .entry(id)\n            .or_default();\n        let end = (offset as usize) + bytes.len();\n        if v.len() < end {\n            v.resize(end, 0);\n        }\n        v[offset as usize..end].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n    }\n\n    fn check_alive(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.crashed {\n            Err(IoError::SimulatedCrash)\n        } else {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn merge(durable: &mut SimMedia, id: FileId, off: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        let v = durable.files.entry(id).or_default();\n        let end = off as usize + bytes.len();\n        if v.len() < end {\n            v.resize(end, 0);\n        }\n        v[off as usize..end].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n    }\n\n    /// Apply the configured crash policy at `point` for a write to `file`.\n    /// `seg` is the in-flight write `(offset, bytes)` whose prefix may be\n    /// retained as a torn write.\n    fn crash(&mut self, point: CrashPoint, file: FileId, seg: Option<(u64, &[u8])>) -> Result<()> {\n        if point != self.policy.at {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // What survives: either nothing, or a prefix of the in-flight write.\n        if let Some((off, bytes)) = seg {\n            if self.policy.torn != Torn::None && !bytes.is_empty() {\n                let n = match self.policy.torn {\n                    Torn::None => 0,\n                    Torn::Half => bytes.len() / 2,\n                    Torn::Short => 137.min(bytes.len().saturating_sub(1)),\n                };\n                if n > 0 {\n                    Self::merge(&mut self.durable, file, off, &bytes[..n]);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Power is lost: the entire page cache (all dirty segments, of every\n        // file) is discarded.\n        self.dirty.clear();\n        self.crashed = true;\n        Err(IoError::SimulatedCrash)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for SimVfs {\n    fn pwrite(&mut self, id: FileId, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        self.check_alive()?;\n        let begin = match id {\n            FileId::Data => CrashPoint::DataWriteBegin,\n            _ => CrashPoint::RootWriteBegin,\n        };\n        // Crash before the first byte hits even the page cache.\n        self.crash(begin, id, Some((offset, data)))?;\n\n        self.dirty\n            .entry(id)\n            .or_default()\n self.crash(end, id, Some((offset, data)))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self, id: FileId) -> Result<()> {\n        self.check_alive()?;\n        let begin = match id {\n            FileId::Data => CrashPoint::DataSyncBegin,\n            _ => CrashPoint::RootSyncBegin,\n        };\n        // A crash as fsync starts: the latest write may be torn on media,\n        // everything else dirty is lost.\n        if begin == self.policy.at {\n            let seg = self\n                .dirty\n                .get(&id)\n                .and_then(|s| s.last())\n                .map(|(o, b)| (*o, b.as_slice()));\n            self.crash(begin, id, seg)?;\n        }\n\n        if let Some(segs) = self.dirty.remove(&id) {\n            for (off, bytes) in &segs {\n                Self::merge(&mut self.durable, id, *off, bytes);\n            }\n        }\n\n        let end = match id {\n            FileId::Data => CrashPoint::DataSyncEnd,\n            _ => CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd,\n        };\n        self.crash(end, id, None)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        self.check_alive()\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, id: FileId) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        self.check_alive()?;\n        Ok(self.durable.file_bytes(id).map(|b| b.to_vec()))\n    }\n\n    fn truncate(&mut self, id: FileId, len: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        self.check_alive()?;\n        let v = self.durable.files.entry(id).or_default();\n        v.resize(len as usize, 0);\n        if v.is_empty() {\n            self.durable.files.remove(&id);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn exists(&self, id: FileId) -> bool {\n        self.durable.files.contains_key(&id)\n    }\n}\n\n// Silence the unused-association warning for CrashPoint::file (kept for\n// documentation/tests of the mapping).\nconst _: fn(CrashPoint) -> FileId = CrashPoint::file;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn policy(at: CrashPoint, torn: Torn) -> CrashPolicy {\n        CrashPolicy::new(at, torn)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn clean_sync_moves_dirty_to_durable() {\n        let no_crash = CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None);\n        let mut v = SimVfs::fresh(no_crash);\n        v.pwrite(FileId::Data, 0, b\"hello\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(v.durable_len(FileId::Data), 0);\n        v.sync(FileId::Data).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(v.durable_bytes(FileId::Data).unwrap(), b\"hello\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn b\"hello\").unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, IoError::SimulatedCrash));\n        let v = v.reopen(policy(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None));\n        assert!(!v.exists(FileId::Data));\n A [`CrashPolicy`] can \"cut the\n//!   power\" at any [`CrashPoint`], optionally retaining only a prefix of the\n//!   in-flight write (torn page / half-page write). Durability model assumed (and what the tests exercise):\n//! * a single `pwrite` may survive torn — any prefix can land, the rest is\n//!   lost;\n//! * bytes written but never `sync`ed may be lost entirely;\n//!   `sync_all` is a barrier — everything before it is durable, and the\n//!   superblock is only written *after* the data sync barrier, which is what\n//!   makes the publish order safe.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// The three files a repository consists of.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum FileId {\n    Data,\n    SbA,\n    SbB,\n}\n\nimpl FileId {\n    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FileId::Data => crate::format::DATA_FILE,\n            FileId::SbA => crate::format::SB_FILE[0],\n            FileId::SbB => crate::format::SB_FILE[1],\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Points in the commit protocol at which power can be cut.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CrashPoint {\n    /// Before any byte of the new data record is written.\n    DataWriteBegin,\n    /// After the data pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    DataWriteEnd,\n    /// At the data fsync call (write still dirty).\n    DataSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the data fsync returns.\n    DataSyncEnd,\n    /// Before any byte of the new superblock page is written.\n    RootWriteBegin,\n    /// After the superblock pwrite returns, before fsync.\n    RootWriteEnd,\n    /// At the superblock fsync call (page still dirty).\n    RootSyncBegin,\n    /// Immediately after the superblock fsync returns.\n    RootSyncEnd,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPoint {\n    pub const ALL: [CrashPoint; 8] = [\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::DataSyncEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootWriteEnd,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncBegin,\n        CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd,\n    ];\n\n    fn file(self) -> FileId {\n        use CrashPoint::*;\n        match self {\n            DataWriteBegin | DataWriteEnd | DataSyncBegin | DataSyncEnd => FileId::Data,\n            RootWriteBegin | RootWriteEnd | RootSyncBegin | RootSyncEnd => FileId::SbA, // slot chosen per-commit\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// How torn the in-flight write is when power is cut mid-write.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Torn {\n    /// No byte survives (write never reached the platter).\n    None,\n    /// Exactly the first half of the write survives.\n    Half,\n    /// A short prefix survives (137 bytes of the 4 KiB page; for data records\n    /// it is clamped inside the record header, i.e. the header itself tears).\n    Short,\n}\n\n/// \"Cut power\" once, at the given point, with the given torn-write behaviour.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CrashPolicy {\n    pub at: CrashPoint,\n    pub torn: Torn,\n}\n\nimpl CrashPolicy {\n    pub fn new(at: CrashPoint, torn: Torn) -> Self {\n        CrashPolicy { at, torn }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum IoError {\n    /// OS-level I/O failure (real backend), or use after a simulated crash.\n    Io(String),\n    /// The configured crash policy fired: the process \"lost power\". Any\n    /// further operation on this VFS instance returns the same error; reboot\n    /// with [`SimVfs::reopen`].\n    SimulatedCrash,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for IoError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            IoError::Io(s) => write!(f, \"io error: {s}\"),\n            IoError::SimulatedCrash => write!(f, \"simulated crash (power lost)\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for IoError {}\n\npub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, IoError>;\n\n/// Minimal storage interface needed by the repository. FileId) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Durably persist directory-entry changes (newly created files).\n    fn sync_dir(&mut self) -> Result<()>;\n    /// Read the whole durable file, or `None` if it does not ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Real filesystem backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct RealVfs {\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl RealVfs {\n    pub fn open(dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self> {\n        let dir = dir.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| IoError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\n        Ok(RealVfs { dir })\n    }\n\n    fn path(&self, id: FileId) -> PathBuf {\n        self.dir.join(id.name())\n    }\n\n One commit appends exactly one data record, then publishes a new\n//! superblock pointing at it:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! 1. pwrite(data.log, tail, record)      // new data sits in the page cache\n//! 2. fsync(data.log)                     // BARRIER: record is durable\n//! 3. pwrite(slot, 0, superblock(page))   // root points at the durable record\n//! 4. fsync(slot)                         // new root is durable -> visible\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The crucial ordering is 2 before 3: a root is never written until the\n//! bytes it references are already on disk. Any crash in steps 1–2 leaves\n//! the old root intact pointing at the old chain; a crash in steps 3–4 tears\n//! the new page (its CRC fails) so the *other*, older slot still recovers.\n//!\n//! ## Recovery selection\n//!\n//! Both 4 KiB superblock pages are decoded and CRC-checked. Every page is\n//! additionally required to reference a valid, fully present record chain:\n//!\n//! * root/data pointers inside the file (`OutOfBounds` otherwise);\n//! * records contiguous and packed from offset 0;\n//! * every header CRC valid;\n//! * generation constant along the chain;\n//! * first record at offset 0 with `prev_off == 0`.\n//!\n//! Among valid candidates the **highest generation** wins; ties break on the\n//! higher slot (slot B was written second in a same-generation tie). Invalid\n//! pages are skipped, so a torn newer page transparently falls back to the\n//! older one. Bytes past the selected chain end are a torn/orphan tail and\n//! are truncated away on open.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\nuse crate::format::{self, Op, RecordHeader, Superblock, but invalid.\n    NoValidSuperblock,\n    /// A (claimed valid) superblock references an invalid record chain.\n    CorruptChain(String),\n    KeyNotFound,\n    Other(String),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Io(e) => write!(f, \"{e}\"),\n            StoreError::Format(e) => write!(f, \"format error: {e}\"),\n            StoreError::NoValidSuperblock => write!(f,\n                \"both superblocks are present but invalid (cannot recover)\"),\n            StoreError::CorruptChain(s) => write!(f, \"corrupt record chain: {s}\"),\n            StoreError::KeyNotFound => write!(f, \"key not found\"),\n            StoreError::Other(s) => write!(f, \"{s}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<IoError> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: IoError) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\nimpl From<format::FormatError> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: format::FormatError) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Format(e)\n    }\n}\n\npub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, StoreError>;\n\n/// {"parentUuid":"07660757-ccce-444d-b83a-f242016d22d4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_grf4fuetmq7nld6ijddjpart","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp1/b/src/demo.rs","content":"//! Deterministic crash-scenario harness, reusable by the CLI (`demo`) and\n//! the HTTP validation endpoints (`/demo/...`).\n//!\n//! {"parentUuid":"52f5f811-0b79-4128-bd14-5a16b8656a21","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_juja6gq58nh7azwleygudp47","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp1/b/src/demo.rs","content":"//! Deterministic crash-scenario harness, reusable by the CLI (`demo`) and\n//! the HTTP validation endpoints (`/demo/...`).\n//!\n//! Every scenario runs against the in-memory [`SimVfs`]: the crash policy is\n//! armed, a commit is attempted, `SimulatedCrash` is swallowed (that is the\n//! point), the media is \"rebooted\" and the repository recovered. What gets\n//! asserted is the recovered generation/key state and the truncation of\n//! orphan bytes — not the crash itself.\n\nuse crate::io::{CrashPoint, CrashPolicy, FileId, IoError, SimVfs, Torn};\nuse crate::repo::{Repository, StoreError};\nuse crate::format::SB_SIZE;\n\n/// Point/torn labels for JSON and CLI.\npub fn parse_point(s: &str) -> Option<CrashPoint> {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    Some(match s {\n        \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => \"DataSyncBegin\",\n        DataSyncEnd => \"DataSyncEnd\",\n        RootWriteBegin => \"RootWriteBegin\",\n        RootWriteEnd => \"RootWriteEnd\",\n        RootSyncBegin => \"RootSyncBegin\",\n        RootSyncEnd => \"RootSyncEnd\",\n    }\n}\n\npub fn parse_torn(s: &str) -> Option<Torn> {\n    Some(match s {\n        \"None\" => Torn::None,\n        \"Half\" => Torn::Half,\n        \"Short\" => Torn::Short,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn torn_name(t: Torn) -> &'static str {\n    match t {\n        Torn::None => \"None\",\n        Torn::Half => \"Half\",\n        Torn::Short => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\n/// after the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this policy\n/// never fires during recovery.\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n    pub opened: bool,\n    pub recovered_generation: Option<u64>,\n    pub expected_generation: u64,\n    pub last_value: Option<String>,\n    pub orphan_bytes_truncated: u64,\n    pub slot_reports: Vec<(u32, bool, bool, String)>,\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl CaseResult {\n    /// Acceptance predicate used by both the CLI and the tests.\n    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        self.opened\n            && self.error.is_none()\n            && self.recovered_generation == Some(self.expected_generation)\n            && self.last_value.as_deref() == Some(match self.expected_generation {\n                2 => \"v2\",\n                3 => \"v3\",\n                1 => \"v1\",\n                _ => return false,\n            })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Publish `rounds - 1` clean generations of key `k` = `v<g>` with the given\n/// policy armed, then attempt one more commit that is allowed to crash.\nfn seed_and_attempt(\n    policy: CrashPolicy,\n    rounds: u64,\n    crashing_value: &str,\n) -> SimVfs {\n    let mut sim = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n    for g in 1..=rounds {\n        let (mut repo, _) =\n            Repository::open(&mut sim as &mut SimVfs2).unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!());\n        let value = if g == rounds {\n            crashing_value\n        } else {\n            Box::leak(format!(\"v{g}\").into_boxed_str())\n        };\n        let res = repo.put(b\"k\".to_vec(), value.as_bytes().to_vec());\n        if g == rounds {\n            // Expected: either committed (barrier already passed) or crash.\n            match res {\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(StoreError::Io(IoError::SimulatedCrash)) => {}\n                Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected error at crash round: {e}\"),\n            }\n            return repo.into_vfs();\n        }\n        res.expect(\"seed commit must succeed\");\n        sim = repo.into_vfs();\n    }\n    sim\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_749e8beaafd448b3e67363fc","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1336,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":56120,"output_tokens":1248,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_juja6gq58nh7azwleygudp47":{"content":"//! Deterministic crash-scenario harness, reusable by the CLI (`demo`) and\n//! the HTTP validation endpoints (`/demo/...`).\n//!\n//! Every scenario runs against the in-memory [`SimVfs`]: the crash policy is\n//! armed, a commit is attempted, `SimulatedCrash` is swallowed (that is the\n//! point), the media is \"rebooted\" and the repository recovered. What gets\n//! asserted is the recovered generation/key state and the truncation of\n//! orphan bytes — not the crash itself.\n\nuse crate::format::Superblock;\nuse crate::io::{CrashPoint, CrashPolicy, FileId, IoError, SimVfs, Torn, SB as _};\nuse crate::repo::{Repository, StoreError};\n\n// re-export SB_SIZE without pulling the whole format namespace at call sites\nmod sb {\n    pub use crate::format::SB_SIZE;\n}\nuse sb::SB_SIZE;\n\n/// Point/torn labels for JSON and CLI.\npub fn parse_point(s: &str) -> Option<CrashPoint> {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    Some(match s {\n        \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => \"DataSyncBegin\",\n        DataSyncEnd => \"DataSyncEnd\",\n        RootWriteBegin => \"RootWriteBegin\",\n        RootWriteEnd => \"RootWriteEnd\",\n        RootSyncBegin => \"RootSyncBegin\",\n        RootSyncEnd => \"RootSyncEnd\",\n    }\n}\n\npub fn parse_torn(s: &str) -> Option<Torn> {\n    Some(match s {\n        \"None\" => Torn::None,\n        \"Half\" => Torn::Half,\n        \"Short\" => Torn::Short,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn torn_name(t: Torn) -> &'static str {\n    match t {\n        Torn::None => \"None\",\n        Torn::Half => \"Half\",\n        Torn::Short => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    // after the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this\n    // policy never fires during recovery.\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n    pub opened: bool,\n    pub recovered_generation: Option<u64>,\n    pub expected_generation: u64,\n    pub v2_present: bool,\n    pub v3_present: bool,\n    pub orphan_bytes_truncated: u64,\n    pub slot_reports: Vec<(u32, bool, String)>,\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl CaseResult {\n    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        self.opened\n            && self.recovered_generation == Some(self.expected_generation)\n            && self.error.is_none()\n            && self.orphan_bytes_truncated == 0\n            // value of the crashed commit must be visible iff it committed\n            && self.v3_present == (self.expected_generation == 3)\n            && !self.v2_present == (self.expected_generation == 3) == false\n            // v2 exists for every recovered state here\n            && self.v2_present\n    }\n}\n\n/// Full matrix: 3 clean commits, crash injected during commit 3, at every\n/// point, with every torn-write variant. After recovery:\n/// * `RootSyncEnd` → commit 3 survived (generation 3, v3 visible);\n/// * every earlier point → rollback to generation 2 (v2 visible, v3 gone),\n///   including torn newer-superblock pages, which fall back to the older\n///   slot; torn data tails are truncated.\npub fn run_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for point in CrashPoint::ALL {\n        for torn in [Torn::None, Torn::Half, Torn::Short] {\n            out.push(run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, torn), 3));\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Same scenario but the crash lands during commit 2 (first alternating\n/// rollback): every point except `RootSyncEnd` must roll back to gen 1.\npub fn run_round2_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for point in CrashPoint::ALL {\n        out.push(run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, Torn::Half), 2));\n    }\n    out\n}\n\nfn run_single(policy: CrashPolicy, crash_round: u64) -> CaseResult {\n    let point = policy.at;\n    let torn = policy.torn;\n    let mut vfs = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n\n    // Publish crash_round-1 clean generations.\n    {\n        let (mut repo, _) = Repository::open(&mut vfs as &mut dyn VfsDyn)\n            .map_err(|_| ())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!(\"fresh open\"));\n    }\n    // The above is intentionally awkward; use the concrete path below.\n    let _ = &mut vfs;\n\n    let mut sim = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n    let pre = crash_round - 1;\n    for g in 1..=pre {\n        let (mut repo, _) = Repository::open(sim_reopenable(&mut sim)).expect(\"open pre\");\n        repo.put(format!(\"k\").into_bytes(), format!(\"v{g}\").into_bytes())\n            .expect(\"pre commit\");\n        // commit needs ownership-free access; rework: Repository borrows vfs\n        let _ = g;\n        todo!()\n    }\n    todo!()\n}\n\n// Repository is generic over V: Vfs; SimVfs is Sized, so we can open\n// Repository<SimVfs> directly and reuse via reopen().\nfn sim_reopenable(_vfs: &mut SimVfs) -> SimVfs {\n    unreachable!()\n}\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1a2fa559-187b-4359-8b3a-f2c00f927f84","session_id":"16e09c12-2279-4a1e-8d8e-59ca184fff1d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp1/b","sessionId":"16e09c12-2279-4a1e-8d8e-59ca184fff1d","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp1-b","slug":"kind-chasing-fountain"}

Deterministic crash-scenario harness, reusable by the CLI (`demo`) and\n//! the HTTP validation endpoints (`/demo/...`).\n//!\n//! Every scenario runs against the in-memory [`SimVfs`]: the crash policy is\n//! armed, a commit is attempted, `SimulatedCrash` is swallowed (that is the\n//! point), the media is \"rebooted\" and the repository recovered. What gets\n//! asserted is the recovered generation/key state and the truncation of\n//! orphan bytes — not the crash itself.\n\nuse crate::format::{Superblock, SB_SIZE};\nuse crate::io::{CrashPoint, CrashPolicy, FileId, IoError, SimVfs, Torn, Vfs};\nuse crate::repo::{Repository, StoreError};\n\npub fn parse_point(s: &str) -> Option<CrashPoint> {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    Some(match s {\n        \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => \"DataSyncBegin\",\n        DataSyncEnd => \"DataSyncEnd\",\n        RootWriteBegin => \"RootWriteBegin\",\n        RootWriteEnd => \"RootWriteEnd\",\n        RootSyncBegin => \"RootSyncBegin\",\n        RootSyncEnd => \"RootSyncEnd\",\n    }\n}\n\npub fn parse_torn(s: &str) -> Option<Torn> {\n    Some(match s {\n        \"None\" => Torn::None,\n        \"Half\" => Torn::Half,\n        \"Short\" => Torn::Short,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn torn_name(t: Torn) -> &'static str {\n    match t {\n        Torn::None => \"None\",\n        Torn::Half => \"Half\",\n        Torn::Short => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\n/// After the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this policy\n/// never fires during recovery.\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n    pub opened: bool,\n    pub recovered_generation: Option<u64>,\n    pub expected_generation: u64,\n    pub last_value: Option<String>,\n    pub orphan_bytes_truncated: u64,\n    /// (slot, present, accepted, detail)\n    pub slot_reports: Vec<(u32, bool, bool, String)>,\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl CaseResult {\n    /// Acceptance predicate used by both the CLI and the tests.\n    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        let want = match self.expected_generation {\n            1 => \"v1\",\n            2 => \"v2\",\n            3 => \"v3\",\n            _ => return false,\n        };\n        self.opened\n            && self.error.is_none()\n            && self.recovered_generation == Some(self.expected_generation)\n            && self.last_value.as_deref() == Some(want)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run one commit-crash-recovery case.\n///\n/// * `rounds` — crash is injected while publishing generation `rounds`;\n/// * key `k` is written as `v1..v{rounds}`; the crashing write is `vC`.\n///\n/// Recovery must select the highest *complete, valid* generation:\n/// generation `rounds` when the crash point is at/past the root barrier,\n/// otherwise `rounds - 1`.\npub fn run_single(policy: CrashPolicy, rounds: u64) -> CaseResult {\n    let point = policy.at;\n    let torn = policy.torn;\n    let committed = point == CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd;\n    let expected = if committed { rounds } else { rounds - 1 };\n\n    // --- seed rounds-1 clean commits, then attempt the crashing one ---\n    let mut sim = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n    for g in 1..=rounds {\n        let (mut repo, _) = Repository::open(sim).expect(\"open before commit\");\n        let value = format!(\"v{}\", if g == rounds { 'C' } else { char::from_digit(g as u32, 10).unwrap() });\n        let res = repo.put(b\"k\".to_vec(), value.into_bytes());\n        sim = repo.into_vfs();\n        match res {\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(StoreError::Io(IoError::SimulatedCrash)) if g == rounds => {}\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected error on round {g}: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- reboot and recover ---\n    let mut reboot = sim.reopen(no_crash());\n    let open = Repository::open(&mut reboot);\n    match open {\n        Ok((repo, report)) => {\n            let last = repo\n                .get(b\"k\")\n                .map(|v| String::from_utf8_lossy(v).into_owned());\n            let slots = report\n                .slots\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (s.slot, s.present, s.accepted, s.detail.clone()))\n                .collect();\n            CaseResult {\n                point: point_name(point),\n                torn: torn_name(torn),\n                crashed_round: rounds,\n                opened: true,\n                recovered_generation: Some(repo.generation()),\n                expected_generation: expected,\n                last_value: last,\n                orphan_bytes_truncated: report.truncated_orphan_bytes,\n                slot_reports: slots,\n                error: None,\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => CaseResult {\n            point: point_name(point),\n            torn: torn_name(torn),\n            crashed_round: rounds,\n            opened: false,\n            recovered_generation: None,\n            expected_generation: expected,\n            last_value: None,\n            orphan_bytes_truncated: 0,\n            slot_reports: Vec::new(),\n            error: Some(e.to_string()),\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n/// 8 points × 3 torn variants, crash during commit 3.\npub fn run_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for point in CrashPoint::ALL {\n        for torn in [Torn::None, Torn::Half, Torn::Short] {\n            out.push(run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, torn), 3));\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Every point with a half-page torn write, crash during commit 2 (the\n/// first rollback, where the older slot is generation 1).\npub fn run_round2_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    CrashPoint::ALL\n        .iter()\n        .map(|&point| run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, Torn::Half), 2))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// The three named acceptance scenarios requested for the delivery.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct NamedScenario {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: String,\n    pub outcome: String,\n    pub report: serde_lite::Json,\n}\n\n// Tiny local JSON value type so the crate stays dependency-free; lives in\n// the http module but reused here via an alias.\nmod serde_lite {\n    use std::fmt::Write;\n\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n    pub enum Json {\n        Null,\n        Bool(bool),\n        Num(f64),\n        Str(String),\n        Arr(Vec<Json>),\n        Obj(Vec<(String, Json)>),\n    }\n\n    impl Json {\n        pub fn s(v: impl Into<String>) -> Json {\n            Json::Str(v.into())\n        }\n        pub fn n(v: u64) -> Json {\n            Json::Num(v as f64)\n        }\n        pub fn escape(buf: &mut String, s: &str) {\n            buf.push('\"');\n            for c in s.chars() {\n                match c {\n                    '\"' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\\\\"\"),\n                    '\\\\' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\\\\\\"),\n                    '\\n' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\n\"),\n                    '\\r' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\r\"),\n                    '\\t' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\t\"),\n                    c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {\n                        let _ = write!(buf, \"\\\\u{:04x}\", c as u32);\n                    }\n                    c => buf.push(c),\n                }\n            }\n            buf.push('\"');\n        }\n\n        pub fn to_string_pretty(&self) -> String {\n            let mut out = String::new();\n            Self::render(self, &mut out, 0);\n            out.push('\\n');\n            out\n        }\n\n        fn render(v: &Json, out: &mut String, indent: usize) {\n            let pad = \"  \".repeat(indent);\n            let pad1 = \"  \".repeat(indent + 1);\n            match v {\n                Json::Null => out.push_str(\"null\"),\n                Json::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { \"true\" } else { \"false\" }),\n                Json::Num(n) => {\n                    if n.fract() == 0.0 {\n                        let _ = write!(out, \"{}\", *n as u64);\n                    } else {\n                        let _ = write!(out, \"{n}\");\n                    }\n                }\n                Json::Str(s) => Self::escape(out, s),\n                Json::Arr(a) => {\n                    if a.is_empty() {\n                        out.push_str(\"[]\");\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    out.push_str(\"[\\n\");\n                    for (i, x) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n                        out.push_str(&pad1);\n                        Self::render(x, out, indent + 1);\n                        if i + 1 < a.len() {\n                            out.push(',');\n                        }\n                        out.push('\\n');\n                    }\n                    out.push_str(&pad);\n                    out.push(']');\n                }\n                Json::Obj(o) => {\n                    if o.is_empty() {\n                        out.push_str(\"{}\");\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    out.push_str(\"{\\n\");\n                    for (i, (k, v)) in o.iter().enumerate() {\n                        out.push_str(&pad1);\n                        Self::escape(out, k);\n                        out.push_str(\": \");\n                        Self::render(v, out, indent + 1);\n  \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\n/// After the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this policy\n/// never fires during recovery.\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        let want = match self.expected_generation {\n            1 => \"v1\",\n            2 => \"v2\",\n            3 => \"v3\",\n            _ => return false,\n }\n}\n\n/// Run one commit-crash-recovery case.\n///\n/// * `rounds` — crash is injected while publishing generation `rounds`;\n/// * key `k` is written as `v1..v{rounds}`; the crashing write is run_single(policy: CrashPolicy, rounds: u64) -> CaseResult {\n    let point = policy.at;\n    let torn = policy.torn;\n    let committed = point == CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd;\n    let expected = if (mut repo, _) = Repository::open(sim).expect(\"open before commit\");\n        let value = format!(\"v{}\", if g == rounds { 'C' } else { char::from_digit(g as u32, 10).unwrap() });\n        let res = {}\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected error on round {g}: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- reboot and recover ---\n    let mut reboot = sim.reopen(no_crash());\n    let open = Every scenario runs against the in-memory [`SimVfs`]: the crash policy is\n//! armed, a commit is attempted, `SimulatedCrash` is swallowed (that is the\n//! point), the media is \"rebooted\" and the repository recovered. What gets\n//! asserted is the recovered generation/key state and the truncation of\n//! orphan bytes — not the crash itself.\n\nuse crate::format::{Superblock, SB_SIZE};\nuse crate::io::{CrashPoint, CrashPolicy, FileId, IoError, SimVfs, Torn, Vfs};\nuse crate::repo::{Repository, StoreError};\n\npub fn parse_point(s: &str) -> Option<CrashPoint> {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    Some(match s {\n        \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => \"DataSyncBegin\",\n        DataSyncEnd => \"DataSyncEnd\",\n        RootWriteBegin => \"RootWriteBegin\",\n        RootWriteEnd => \"RootWriteEnd\",\n        RootSyncBegin => \"RootSyncBegin\",\n        RootSyncEnd => \"RootSyncEnd\",\n    }\n}\n\npub fn parse_torn(s: &str) -> Option<Torn> {\n    Some(match s {\n        \"None\" => Torn::None,\n        \"Half\" => Torn::Half,\n        \"Short\" => Torn::Short,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn torn_name(t: Torn) -> &'static str {\n    match t {\n        Torn::None => \"None\",\n        Torn::Half => \"Half\",\n        Torn::Short => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\n/// After the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this policy\n/// never fires during recovery.\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n    pub opened: bool,\n    pub recovered_generation: Option<u64>,\n    pub expected_generation: u64,\n    pub last_value: Option<String>,\n    pub orphan_bytes_truncated: u64,\n    /// (slot, present, accepted, detail)\n    pub slot_reports: Vec<(u32, bool, bool, String)>,\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl CaseResult {\n    /// Acceptance predicate used by both the CLI and the tests.\n    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        let want = match self.expected_generation {\n            1 => \"v1\",\n            2 => \"v2\",\n            3 => \"v3\",\n            _ => return false,\n        };\n        self.opened\n            && self.error.is_none()\n            && self.recovered_generation == Some(self.expected_generation)\n            && self.last_value.as_deref() == Some(want)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run one commit-crash-recovery case.\n///\n/// * `rounds` — crash is injected while publishing generation `rounds`;\n/// * key `k` is written as `v1..v{rounds}`; the crashing write is `vC`.\n///\n/// Recovery must select the highest *complete, valid* generation:\n/// generation `rounds` when the crash point is at/past the root barrier,\n/// otherwise `rounds - 1`.\npub fn run_single(policy: CrashPolicy, rounds: u64) -> CaseResult {\n    let point = policy.at;\n    let torn = policy.torn;\n    let committed = point == CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd;\n    let expected = if committed { rounds } else { rounds - 1 };\n\n    // --- seed rounds-1 clean commits, then attempt the crashing one ---\n    let mut sim = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n    for g in 1..=rounds {\n        let (mut repo, _) = Repository::open(sim).expect(\"open before commit\");\n        let value = format!(\"v{}\", if g == rounds { 'C' } else { char::from_digit(g as u32, 10).unwrap() });\n        let res = repo.put(b\"k\".to_vec(), value.into_bytes());\n        sim = repo.into_vfs();\n        match res {\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(StoreError::Io(IoError::SimulatedCrash)) if g == rounds => {}\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected error on round {g}: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- reboot and recover ---\n    let mut reboot = sim.reopen(no_crash());\n    let open = Repository::open(&mut reboot);\n    match open {\n        Ok((repo, report)) => {\n            let last = repo\n                .get(b\"k\")\n                .map(|v| String::from_utf8_lossy(v).into_owned());\n            let slots = report\n                .slots\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (s.slot, s.present, s.accepted, s.detail.clone()))\n                .collect();\n            CaseResult {\n                point: point_name(point),\n                torn: torn_name(torn),\n                crashed_round: rounds,\n                opened: true,\n                recovered_generation: Some(repo.generation()),\n                expected_generation: expected,\n                last_value: last,\n                orphan_bytes_truncated: report.truncated_orphan_bytes,\n                slot_reports: slots,\n                error: None,\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => CaseResult {\n            point: point_name(point),\n            torn: torn_name(torn),\n            crashed_round: rounds,\n            opened: false,\n            recovered_generation: None,\n            expected_generation: expected,\n            last_value: None,\n            orphan_bytes_truncated: 0,\n            slot_reports: Vec::new(),\n            error: Some(e.to_string()),\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n/// 8 points × 3 torn variants, crash during commit 3.\npub fn run_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for point in CrashPoint::ALL {\n        for torn in [Torn::None, Torn::Half, Torn::Short] {\n            out.push(run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, torn), 3));\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Every point with a half-page torn write, crash during commit 2 (the\n/// first rollback, where the older slot is generation 1).\npub fn run_round2_matrix() -> Vec<CaseResult> {\n    CrashPoint::ALL\n        .iter()\n        .map(|&point| run_single(CrashPolicy::new(point, Torn::Half), 2))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// The three named acceptance scenarios requested for the delivery.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct NamedScenario {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: String,\n    pub outcome: String,\n    pub report: serde_lite::Json,\n}\n\n// Tiny local JSON value type so the crate stays dependency-free; lives in\n// the http module but reused here via an alias.\nmod serde_lite {\n    use std::fmt::Write;\n\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n    pub enum Json {\n        Null,\n        Bool(bool),\n        Num(f64),\n        Str(String),\n        Arr(Vec<Json>),\n        Obj(Vec<(String, Json)>),\n    }\n\n    impl Json {\n        pub fn s(v: impl Into<String>) -> Json {\n            Json::Str(v.into())\n        }\n        pub fn n(v: u64) -> Json {\n            Json::Num(v as f64)\n        }\n        pub fn escape(buf: &mut String, s: &str) {\n            buf.push('\"');\n            for c in s.chars() {\n                match c {\n                    '\"' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\\\\"\"),\n                    '\\\\' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\\\\\\"),\n                    '\\n' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\n\"),\n                    '\\r' => buf.push_str(\"\\\\r\"),\n                 c => buf.push(c),\n                }\n            }\n            buf.push('\"');\n        }\n\n        pub fn to_string_pretty(&self) -> String {\n            let mut out = String::new();\n            Self::render(self, &mut out, 0);\n            out.push('\\n');\n            out\n        }\n\n        fn render(v: &Json, out: &mut String, indent: usize) {\n            let pad = \"  \".repeat(indent);\n            let pad1 = \"  \".repeat(indent + 1);\n            match v {\n                Json::Null => out.push_str(\"null\"),\n                Json::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { \"true\" } else { \"false\" }),\n                Json::Num(n) => {\n                    if n.fract() == 0.0 {\n                        let _ = write!(out, \"{}\", *n as u64);\n Json::Arr(a) => {\n                    if a.is_empty() {\n                        out.push_str(\"[]\");\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    out.push_str(\"[\\n\");\n                    for (i, x) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n                        out.push_str(&pad1);\n                        Self::render(x, out, indent + 1);\n out.push_str(&pad);\n                    out.push(']');\n                }\n                Json::Obj(o) => {\n                    if o.is_empty() {\n                        out.push_str(\"{}\");\n Deterministic crash-scenario harness, reusable by the CLI (`demo`) and\n//! the HTTP validation endpoints (`/demo/...`).\n//!\n//! Every scenario runs against the in-memory [`SimVfs`]: the crash policy is\n//! armed, a commit is attempted, `SimulatedCrash` is swallowed (that is the\n//! point), the media is \"rebooted\" and the repository recovered. What gets\n//! asserted is the recovered generation/key state and the truncation of\n//! orphan bytes — not the crash itself.\n\nuse crate::io::{CrashPoint, CrashPolicy, FileId, IoError, SimVfs, Torn};\nuse crate::repo::{Repository, StoreError};\nuse crate::format::SB_SIZE;\n\n/// Point/torn labels for JSON and CLI.\npub fn parse_point(s: &str) -> Option<CrashPoint> {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    Some(match s {\n        \"DataWriteBegin\" => DataWriteBegin,\n        \"DataWriteEnd\" => DataWriteEnd,\n        \"DataSyncBegin\" => DataSyncBegin,\n        \"DataSyncEnd\" => DataSyncEnd,\n        \"RootWriteBegin\" => RootWriteBegin,\n        \"RootWriteEnd\" => RootWriteEnd,\n        \"RootSyncBegin\" => RootSyncBegin,\n        \"RootSyncEnd\" => RootSyncEnd,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn point_name(p: CrashPoint) -> &'static str {\n    use CrashPoint::*;\n    match p {\n        DataWriteBegin => \"DataWriteBegin\",\n        DataWriteEnd => \"DataWriteEnd\",\n        DataSyncBegin => \"DataSyncBegin\",\n        DataSyncEnd => \"DataSyncEnd\",\n        RootWriteBegin => \"RootWriteBegin\",\n        RootWriteEnd => \"RootWriteEnd\",\n        RootSyncBegin => \"RootSyncBegin\",\n        RootSyncEnd => \"RootSyncEnd\",\n    }\n}\n\npub fn parse_torn(s: &str) -> Option<Torn> {\n    Some(match s {\n        \"None\" => Torn::None,\n        \"Half\" => Torn::Half,\n        \"Short\" => Torn::Short,\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\npub fn torn_name(t: Torn) -> &'static str {\n    match t {\n        Torn::None => \"None\",\n        Torn::Half => \"Half\",\n        Torn::Short => \"Short\",\n    }\n}\n\n/// after the root barrier there is nothing left to crash on, so this policy\n/// never fires during recovery.\nfn no_crash() -> CrashPolicy {\n    CrashPolicy::new(CrashPoint::RootSyncEnd, Torn::None)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CaseResult {\n    pub point: &'static str,\n    pub torn: &'static str,\n    pub crashed_round: u64,\n    pub opened: bool,\n    pub recovered_generation: Option<u64>,\n    pub expected_generation: u64,\n    pub last_value: Option<String>,\n    pub orphan_bytes_truncated: u64,\n    pub slot_reports: Vec<(u32, bool, bool, String)>,\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl CaseResult {\n    /// Acceptance predicate used by both the CLI and the tests.\n    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool {\n        self.opened\n            && self.error.is_none()\n            && self.recovered_generation == Some(self.expected_generation)\n            && self.last_value.as_deref() == Some(match self.expected_generation {\n                2 => \"v2\",\n                3 => \"v3\",\n                1 => \"v1\",\n                _ => return false,\n            })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Publish `rounds - 1` clean generations of key `k` = `v<g>` with the given\n/// policy armed, then attempt one more commit that is allowed to crash.\nfn seed_and_attempt(\n    policy: CrashPolicy,\n    rounds: u64,\n    crashing_value: &str,\n) -> SimVfs {\n    let mut sim = SimVfs::fresh(policy);\n    for g in 1..=rounds {\n        let (mut repo, _) =\n            Repository::open(&mut sim as &mut SimVfs2).unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!());\n        let value = if g == rounds {\n            crashing_value\n        } else {\n            Box::leak(format!(\"v{g}\").into_boxed_str())\n        };\n        let res = repo.put(b\"k\".to_vec(), value.as_bytes().to_vec());\n        if g == rounds {\n            // Expected: either committed (barrier already passed) or crash.\n            match res {\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(StoreError::Io(IoError::SimulatedCrash)) => {}\n                Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected error at crash round: {e}\"),\n            }\n            return repo.into_vfs();\n        }\n        res.expect(\"seed commit must succeed\");\n        sim = repo.into_vfs();\n    }\n    sim\n}\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fd9dcace-d397-4888-b8f8-3d6872e01e4e","session_id":"16e09c12-2279-4a1e-8d8e-59ca184fff1d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp1/b","sessionId":"16e09c12-2279-4a1e-8d8e-59ca184fff1d","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp1-b","slug":"kind-chasing-fountain"}
